clue.text: Fellow is holding paper that is in one hundred parts?

indicators.note: holding means the word is wraps around the paper and 'that is' pieces

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Someone tearing a sheet of paper into a hundred pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: two fifties make one hundred, so fifties can be thought of as parts of a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Two notes or amounts of fifty each make up a hundred, so they are its parts.

clue.text: Data supply, rapid, obtained for BBC sports

indicators.note: sports here is a verb, to wear or show off, read as playing around with the letters

explanation.surface: Fast internet obtained so the BBC's sports coverage can be watched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' looks like the BBC's sports output, but it signals rearranging RAPID OBTAINED FOR BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast cable internet is a service that delivers data to homes.

clue.text: Without hypocrisy, Ben's mother/father stupidly welcoming German swine

indicators.note: welcoming means the jumbled letters take the German and swine pieces inside
stupidly means the letters of Ben's, mother and father are jumbled foolishly

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name
mofo is coarse American slang for a contemptible person, a swine

explanation.surface: Ben's parent foolishly lets in a German pig, a farmyard farce.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash just separates the two parents' words, both of which go into the jumble with BENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something with total sincerity is the opposite of hypocrisy; the idiom means wholeheartedly.

clue.text: I I had turned into I I

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: turned means the contraction of 'I had' is read backwards

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A puzzling string of first-person pronouns, like a grammar exercise gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The first I is the chemical symbol, the definition. The last two give I and ONE (I as a numeral), and DI goes into them.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical symbol I stands for the halogen element number 53.

clue.text: Fake drug injected by struggling salon worker?

parts.note: a sham is a fake

indicators.note: injected by means the drug letter is put inside the struggling word

parts.note: struggling financially means poor
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A hard-up hairdresser being dosed with counterfeit drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser's assistant who washes customers' hair works in a salon.

clue.text: Root around parts from centre

indicators.note: parts means the from-centre word is split open to take the around letter

parts.note: radial means spreading out from a centre
C is circa, around

explanation.surface: Digging around a plant's root parts from the middle outwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun but it is a verb: RADIAL parts to let in C.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a radical is a root, as in square root; botanically it also pertains to roots.

clue.text: One old vehicle in road, broadcasting family AOR station

indicators.note: in means the one, old and vehicle pieces sit inside the jumbled road
broadcasting means scattering, so the letters of road are spread about

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a car is a vehicle
a line is a family lineage

explanation.surface: A family in an old car on the road, listening to a rock station.
explanation.walkthrough: AOR is album-oriented rock, the format this famous former pirate station adopted.
explanation.definitionFit: The offshore pirate station of the 1960s now broadcasts album-oriented rock music.

clue.text: Pop covers have 50% lost in transfer from server

indicators.note: covers means the pop word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a father, dad
to own is to have

indicators.note: 50% means the first half of the word lost is kept

explanation.surface: Pop song covers half lost in a file transfer from a server.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop covers' suggests songs, but Pop is DAD, holding OWN and LO.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying a file from a remote computer to your own is the computing sense of the word.

clue.text: Event allowing seconds to be put out?

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of allowing seconds are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop sale that lets slightly flawed goods be sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' are flawed goods, and a shop that is shutting puts out its remaining stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop shutting for good holds a special event selling off all its stock cheaply.

clue.text: Small bricks on top of one

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of one, this being a down clue

explanation.surface: Stacking small bricks on top of one another.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish toy consists of small interlocking plastic building bricks.

clue.text: See 1
See 11
To page 13 in Bradbury book

parts.note: 13 across gives PEEL, so the clue holds TO PAGE PEEL IN, a jumble of the title's first two words; Bradbury book is the definition

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn to page 13 in a Bradbury novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: read as an instruction, the title says its first two words are scrambled, and TO PAGE PEEL IN is that scramble, with 13 standing for its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm Bradbury's first novel, a 1959 campus satire, has this title.

clue.text: Tyneside location's chasing glossy minerals

parts.note: a glossy is a magazine, a mag
Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
a site is a location
the 's of location's

explanation.surface: A spot on Tyneside chasing shiny mineral deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesite is a magnesium carbonate mineral; the plural gives several samples.

clue.text: See 18
Mata goal is seen as foul, causing rare pain

indicators.note: a foul is an illegal move, and foul also means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer's goal judged a foul, causing pain to fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Juan Mata is a Spanish footballer; the word is rare enough to be missing from many dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare medical term names bodily pain, from Greek soma, body, and algos, ache.

clue.text: A stomach upset's come through pleasant activity

indicators.note: through means the come piece is inside the reversed stomach word
upset in a down clue turns the stomach word upside down

parts.note: tum is informal for stomach
come is vulgar slang for semen

explanation.surface: An upset stomach getting through a pleasant pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment or fun is enjoyable pastime, such as a fairground ride.

clue.text: See 5
Pagan words at the altar, possibly our last

parts.note: I do is said at a wedding service

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of our last could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Vows at a wedding altar that may be our final ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipping idols marks one as heathen, a non-Christian believer.

clue.text: DJ spinning record New Hearts penned by US singer

indicators.note: penned by means held inside the singer's name

parts.note: Billy Joel is an American singer

indicators.note: spinning means the record, new and hearts pieces are turned round together

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
H is hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A DJ spinning a new record by the band Hearts, written by an American singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The US singer is Billy Joel; Hearts is the card suit abbreviation, not a band.
explanation.definitionFit: The Radio 1 presenter was Britain's most celebrated champion of new music on air.

clue.text: Influenced by potting the plant

indicators.note: potting means putting the into the influenced-by phrase, as a plant is put in a pot

parts.note: a la means in the style of, influenced by

explanation.surface: A gardener swayed by potting the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh mallow genus, and the rose of Sharon shrub, are both flowering garden species.

clue.text: Perhaps love conditions in which Ben Fogle's heading off again?

indicators.note: in which means the remaining letters go inside the conditions word

parts.note: strings are conditions, as in no strings attached

indicators.note: again here signals the letters being reworked once more
heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Ben Fogle is a British TV presenter and adventurer; his first name loses its head

explanation.surface: Love making Ben Fogle set off on another adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' rearranges ENFOGLE, which goes inside STRINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is an example of an intense emotion, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Good army film

parts.note: a host is an army, as in heavenly host

explanation.surface: Praising a good war film.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1990 romantic fantasy movie starred Patrick Swayze and Demi Moore.

clue.text: Snake's breath

definitions.meaning: to snake is to twist and turn, as a path does
to get your breath back is to recover your puff

explanation.surface: A snake's breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A road meanders and twists; breath is air in the lungs, as in 'winded'.

clue.text: I'll go for both feet

parts.note: saying I'll go for something amounts to I am for it, giving I AM
bi- is a prefix meaning two or both

explanation.surface: Someone choosing to do both feet, perhaps in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrical units of verse of a short then long syllable are poetic feet.

clue.text: See 2
Fault line's split — head off

indicators.note: split means the fault word opens to take the line letter

parts.note: a defect is a fault

explanation.surface: A geological fault line splitting, with the headland breaking off.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert or turn something aside before it arrives is to stave it off.

clue.text: Playwright, mostly oblique

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: traverse as an old adjective means lying across, slanting

explanation.surface: A dramatist who is, for the most part, indirect.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of the 1920s and 30s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Travers was an English dramatist famous for stage farces such as Rookery Nook.
